correctness.rationale: Forest determinant/matching identity and finite-walk adjugate identity proved. Complete all-tree order-eight-and-below Prüfer cross-check and exact rational Bernstein-type coefficient sign tests cover every adjacent pair; 2 exceptional n=8 pairs each show opposite sign at two rational spectral-admissible attenuation values, verified by exact fractions and fourth-walk norm bounds. Computation is finite and exhaustive only through order eight.

originality.rationale: Original Katz definition and endpoint interpolation are known. Inspected Benzi–Klymko 2013 and Aprahamian–Higham–Higham 2015 cover general limits/parameter matching, not exact minimal tree size and minimal adjacent-pair classification. Distinct questions of graph-edge perturbation and fixed-parameter computational ranking do not imply the claim; targeted searches of indexed mathematical literature showed no duplicate. The residual possibility of an unindexed equivalence remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional, as unindexed or unavailable graph-centrality literature may prove the same sharp threshold.
Only the Katz uniform-baseline convention is covered; normalized, directed, weighted or other attenuation schemes can behave differently.

value.rationale: The smallest tree admitting an adjacent-vertex Katz ranking reversal is a natural sharp network-science boundary. Identifying both and only both minimal topologies makes the answer structurally informative, beyond a single contrived numerical sign flip. It isolates a failure of degree-based local ranking under global walk effects and supplies reusable finite counterexamples.
